nom: 1.8% Salicylic Acid Acne Spot Treatment Drying Lotion

segments.sensitive: Several reviewers with sensitive skin, including ones who call it 'very sensitive' or 'super sensitive,' report no irritation or burning even when treating individual spots.
segments.oily: The one reviewer with oily skin reports it works well, leaving skin soft and not sticky.

concerns.dehydration: The lotion is designed to dry out treated spots, and most reviewers see this as expected and localized, sometimes recommending a moisturizer afterward; a couple of reviewers, however, felt it dried their skin without actually clearing the blemish, and one warns it may not suit already-dry skin.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers report a clear reduction in redness around blemishes, often visible by the next morning; one reviewer, however, says redness stuck around longer than she expected.
concerns.barrier: The large majority of reviewers, including several with sensitive skin, report no irritation, itching, or burning from the treatment; the only exception noted is a slight sting when applied to already-broken skin.
concerns.spots: Reports are mixed: some reviewers say it reduced dark marks and post-acne pigmentation within one to two weeks, while one reviewer says it made no difference to her dark spots at all.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers report smaller, flatter, less inflamed pimples within one to a few nights of spot treatment; a few reviewers, however, say it only somewhat helped, working inconsistently or doing little for more severe, 'hardcore' acne.

aspects.libelle: Dries visibly white or chalky, night use only
Small bottle goes a long way
Noticeable medicinal or sulfur scent for some

extraits.titre: Around $58 per ounce. Fussy to apply.
extraits.texte: I don't get it. Why do you have to mess with keeping ingredients separated rather than just making a product that comes in two separate bottles? Let's break this down. Does it moisturize? Uhhh, no. If anything, it dries it out, hence "drying lotion". Does it get rid of dark spots? No, not in my experience. Does it help clear up acne? Somewhat. Does it irritate my skin? No. I can't say it did much other than sort of drying out acne, but I can't say it really did a lot for hardcore acne. Does it smell? Meh, not much. Nothing noticeable to me. Is it worth the money? No. I get better results from a cream that costs half of what this does, and I don't have to mess with separated ingredients and swabs. Is it a large bottle? No. And at around $58 PER OUNCE (at the time of ordering), it is only slightly less than pure silver. Conclusion: the price is insane, especially when you consider it does nothing for dark spots, and very little for acne. Then, when you consider all the fru-fru fuss required to apply it, they should pay me to use this. I would not reorder. It may work for some, but it's a pointless mess for me.

I had high hopes for this, but it didn’t really deliver. The powder took an unusually long time to separate from the liquid, which made it frustrating to use since you’re not supposed to shake it. Even once I managed to apply it, the results were underwhelming. My pimples didn’t shrink much, and redness stuck around longer than expected. It also felt a bit drying without actually clearing anything up. I did not notice any skin irritation which is a plus! Overall, it might work for others, but for me it was slow, inconvenient, and not very effective. The scent however was pleasant.

Only works sometimes. It dies fast, but flakes off really easily and does not last the night when it’s supposed to. I haven’t noticed much of a difference in scars, but it has reduced swelling. Does not clear the acne completely, only reduces it.

extraits.titre: Simple, Effective Spot Treatment That Does What It Says
extraits.texte: I get the occasional small zit right around the time of the month, and this Dr. Leo 1.8% salicylic acid drying lotion has been great for those spots. It’s not miracle magic and it doesn’t claim to be but it does exactly what it’s supposed to. I apply a tiny amount directly to the blemish before bed, and overnight it helps calm the redness and size. After a few days it’s almost gone, which is exactly the kind of predictable result I’m looking for from a spot treatment. This works differently from pimple patches. Pimple patches physically cover a spot with a soft, adhesive hydrocolloid that absorbs fluid and protects the area from picking and external irritants. They’re great if you want a protective barrier and quick flattening of a blemish. This salicylic acid lotion, on the other hand, chemically exfoliates. The salicylic acid works to unclog pores and dissolve the buildup inside a blemish, so you’re treating it from the inside out rather than covering it from the outside. Both have their uses, but I like having this lotion on hand for occasional breakouts because it feels more like a traditional acne treatment and doesn’t leave anything asvisible on the skin like a patch does. I have sensitive skin and didn’t experience irritation or burning when I used this as directed. It dries down quickly and doesn’t feel greasy or heavy, so I can put it on at night and not worry about it transferring to my pillow. I appreciate that it’s targeted and simple — no complicated routines, ju

Here I am excited about this product that pulled the hair out of its follicle. I have very sensitive skin and it wasn’t irritated after application. It was very easy to use and worth way more than the suggested price. It’s not greasy and comes with an applicator
I loved this product! It leaves my skin soft after application, it's not sticky, and you can see the effects from the first use. It's great for oily skin.
Is majorly helping get rid of post acne pigmentation!/ reducing the look. Doesn’t prevent acne. Easy to use and worth it!
